bottom_line: In patients with a recent acute coronary syndrome, rivaroxaban vs placebo reduced the primary composite of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke (8.9% vs. 10.7%; hazard ratio 0.84; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.96).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population, rivaroxaban (combined doses) vs placebo reduced the composite of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke (8.9% vs. 10.7%; hazard ratio 0.84; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.96) while increasing TIMI major bleeding not related to CABG (2.1% vs. 0.6%) and intracranial hemorrhage (0.6% vs. 0.2%); the document reports no significant difference in fatal bleeding (0.3% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.66).

major_points.text: Double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial in recent acute coronary syndrome patients testing low-dose rivaroxaban twice daily (2.5 mg or 5 mg) vs placebo.
major_points.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, we randomly assigned 15,526 patients with a recent acute coronary syndrome to receive twice-daily doses of either 2.5 mg or 5 mg of rivaroxaban or placebo

major_points.text: Primary efficacy endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke.

major_points.text: Rivaroxaban reduced the primary efficacy endpoint compared with placebo.
major_points.quote: Rivaroxaban significantly reduced the primary efficacy end point, as compared with placebo, with respective rates of 8.9% and 10.7% (hazard ratio in the rivaroxaban group, 0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.96; P = 0.008)

major_points.text: Rivaroxaban increased major bleeding not related to CABG and intracranial hemorrhage vs placebo, without significant increase in fatal bleeding.
major_points.quote: As compared with placebo, rivaroxaban increased the rates of major bleeding not related to coronary-artery bypass grafting (2.1% vs. 0.6%, P<0.001) and intracranial hemorrhage (0.6% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.009), without a significant increase in fatal bleeding (0.3% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.66)

major_points.text: The 2.5-mg twice-daily dose (vs placebo) reduced cardiovascular and all-cause mortality; this survival benefit was not seen with the 5-mg dose.
major_points.quote: The twice-daily 2.5-mg dose of rivaroxaban reduced the rates of death from cardiovascular causes (2.7% vs. 4.1%, P = 0.002) and from any cause (2.9% vs. 4.5%, P = 0.002), a survival benefit that was not seen with the twice-daily 5-mg dose.

absolute_effects.text: Primary efficacy endpoint occurred in 8.9% with rivaroxaban vs 10.7% with placebo.
absolute_effects.quote: Rivaroxaban significantly reduced the primary efficacy end point, as compared with placebo, with respective rates of 8.9% and 10.7%

absolute_effects.text: TIMI major bleeding not related to CABG occurred in 2.1% with rivaroxaban vs 0.6% with placebo.
absolute_effects.quote: rivaroxaban increased the rates of major bleeding not related to coronary-artery bypass grafting (2.1% vs. 0.6%, P<0.001)

absolute_effects.text: Intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 0.6% with rivaroxaban vs 0.2% with placebo.
Number needed to treat statement: composite end point prevented in 1 patient if 56 patients treated for 2 years with rivaroxaban.
absolute_effects.quote: the composite end point would be prevented in 1 patient if 56 patients were treated for 2 years with rivaroxaban.

subgroups.text: Results were examined according to major subgroups for general consistency of treatment effect, with interaction testing performed.
subgroups.quote: Results were examined according to major subgroups for general consistency of treat- ment effect, and interaction testing was per- formed.

subgroups.text: Primary efficacy endpoint effect was consistent among subgroups except for patients with a history of stroke or transient ischemic attack.
subgroups.quote: The reduction in the primary efficacy end point with rivaroxaban             was consistent among the subgroups except for              patients with a history of stroke or transient is­          chemic attack

subgroups.text: Subgroup results table includes history of stroke or TIA (hazard ratio 1.57; 95% CI 0.75–3.31).

harms.text: Intracranial hemorrhage was higher with rivaroxaban than placebo.
Fatal bleeding did not significantly differ between rivaroxaban and placebo in the combined comparison.
harms.quote: There was no significant difference in the rates of fatal bleed- ing associated with rivaroxaban as compared with placebo (0.3% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.66).

harms.text: Premature discontinuation of treatment occurred in similar proportions across groups; most common reasons for discontinuation of rivaroxaban were adverse events and patients’ choice.
harms.quote: premature discontinuation of treatment occurred in 26.9% of patients receiving the 2.5-mg dose of rivaroxa- ban, 29.4% receiving the 5-mg dose of rivaroxaban, and 26.4% receiving placebo. The most common reasons for discontinuation of rivaroxaban were adverse events and patients’ choice.

inclusion_criteria.quote: Enrollment occurred within 7 days after hospital admission for an acute coronary syndrome.

inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients who were under 55 years of age had either diabetes mellitus or a previous myo- cardial infarction in addition to the index event.

analysis_methods.text: Prespecified efficacy analyses used a modified intention-to-treat approach with censoring rules tied to treatment phase and discontinuation.
analysis_methods.quote: As prespecified, efficacy analyses were performed with the use of a modified intention-to-treat ap- proach, which included the randomized patients and the end-point events that occurred after ran- domization

analysis_methods.text: Primary safety analysis included patients randomized who received at least one dose, assessed from first dose until 2 days after stopping study drug.
analysis_methods.quote: The primary safety analysis included all patients who underwent randomiza- tion and who received at least one dose of a study drug, with evaluation performed from the time of administration of the first dose of a study drug un- til 2 days after the discontinuation

analysis_methods.text: Primary comparison used stratified log-rank test at alpha 0.05 based on intention to use a thienopyridine; closed testing procedure for dose comparisons.
analysis_methods.quote: at an alpha level of 0.05 on the basis of the log-rank test, stratified according to the intention to use a thienopyridine. If this comparison significantly favored rivarox- aban, then each of the two doses of rivaroxaban was simultaneously compared

analysis_methods.text: Power based on accruing 983 primary efficacy end-point events, providing ~96% power to detect 22.5% relative reduction for combined-dose vs placebo.
analysis_methods.quote: We determined that a total of 983 primary efficacy end-point events would provide a power of approximately 96% to detect a 22.5% relative reduction between the combined-dose group re­ ceiving rivaroxaban and the placebo group

criticisms.quote: Among the patients who had a history of stroke or transient ischemic attack, 198 received aspirin only and 217 received aspirin and a thienopyridine. The latter was a deviation from the study protocol.
